target_customer: Dog owners paying through partner vet clinics and mobile vets, starting in San Francisco and New York; cats planned
problem: Cancer in dogs is usually found late; a blood based liquid biopsy could detect cancer signals early and monitor dogs through treatment.
business_model: Consumer and vet clinic diagnostic test sold per test and as annual screening with baseline banking; monitoring for dogs in treatment

founders.name: Ming-Shan Tsai
education: University of Oxford, DPhil in Zoology
previous_startups: ZYTCA (AI digital pathology for vet clinics in China; launch post says it raised $3.3M; outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page credits an AI digital pathology system distributed to 10,000+ vet clinics in China.

founders.name: Bin Li
prior_employers: University of Oxford (postdoctoral researcher, AI precision medicine, cancer imaging, pathology)
founders.background_notes: Per company site; YC launch post describes him as an Oxford machine learning scientist. Whether the YC page lists him as a founder was not confirmed beyond the launch post and company site.

competitors.name: PetDx OncoK9
competitors.what: Blood based multi-cancer early detection liquid biopsy for dogs using NGS
competitors.traction_then: Commercial since 2021 launch and validated in the CANDiD study

competitors.name: CanCan Diagnostics K9-LiquiDX
competitors.what: Edinburgh spinout liquid biopsy for monitoring canine cancer progression
competitors.funding_then: pre-seed from Advanced Genomics Limited and a private investor

competitors.name: IDEXX Cancer Dx
competitors.traction_then: Discussed in an October 2026 dvm360 podcast

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-modal cell-free DNA sequencing (fragmentation, copy number, 5mC and 5hmC methylation) needs wet lab, sequencing and ML work; the launch post reports 896 samples from 341 dogs and 91% sensitivity and 95% specificity, company reported.

defensibility.rationale: Sample cohort and models take time to build, but a well funded rival (PetDx) already has a commercial test; no patents were found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established players already sell canine cancer blood tests; no acquisition of Canos reported.

market_need_then: Owners pay for pet care and a commercial canine liquid biopsy (OncoK9) has existed since 2021; the company reports over 160 attendees from 130 clinics at New York Vet and 10 founding clinics onboarding (launch post, self reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses canos.ai; acquisition details not found

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and consumer facing: human-grade cancer monitoring for your furry family

brand_strength.rationale: Own site and YC launch post only; the name appears to nod to canine but no source states it.

outcome_analysis: Canos is an active Fall 2026 YC company from Oxford founders with veterinary diagnostics experience, selling cell-free DNA cancer screening and monitoring for dogs. Funding beyond YC is not public. It faces an established competitor (PetDx) and must prove clinical value and distribution through vet clinics, which are the main risks.
notes: Unverified: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with San Francisco headquarters, on a page containing AI generated text; a single aggregator so not recorded as a round. The YC page says team size 0 in the dataset. ZYTCA funding of $3.3M comes from the Canos launch post only. Founded year 2026 per YC. Completeness pass: the $125k seed is now recorded as a round, resting on a single database (Dealroom, no date or investors); it may be YC's standard deal. Press search found no announced round.
